title: Jagged Smoked Irish Fish Stew
description: A hearty, mustardy Irish fish stew with a smoky and spicy kick, featuring Thai fish sauce and chewy fish, perfect for a sick day, and made in a Korean brass bowl, this dish is also Buddhist-temple-friendly.
instructions: Rinse the cod fillets under cold water, pat dry with paper towels, and set aside.
Heat the chicken broth in a large Korean brass bowl over medium heat until it starts to simmer.
Add the smoked paprika, Thai fish sauce, and Dijon mustard to the broth, whisking until well combined.
Add the chopped onions, sliced carrots, and chopped celery to the broth, cooking until the vegetables are tender.
Add the diced potatoes to the broth, cooking for an additional 10 minutes, or until they are tender.
Add the cod fillets to the broth, cooking for an additional 5 minutes, or until they are cooked through.
Stir in the heavy cream, and cook for an additional 2 minutes, or until the stew is heated through.
Season the stew with salt and pepper to taste, then serve hot.
